headline: H0 REFUTED: the shipped +/-5% per-part mass envelope CANNOT defeat Flory-Stockmayer gelability for any of the 7 first-principles DGEBA+amine envelopes -- the full worst-case stoichiometric-index excursion (+10.5263%/-9.5238%) stays strictly inside the 1/((f-1)(g-1)) <= r <= (f-1)(g-1) window (7/7, verdict invariant over the commercial EEW 182-192 spec band). The documented envelope->index gap is therefore a conversion/Tg-quality concern, NOT a network-formation risk. The envelope shifts the gel-point epoxide conversion by exactly +5.1315%/-4.8810% (EEW/AHEW/g-invariant sqrt corollary), and the per-part band would have to grow to P* (binding envelope reported; minimum across 7) before touching the gelation cliff.
hypothesis_H0: The shipped 3-constraint +/-5% per-part mass envelope can push a nominally-formulated two-part epoxy-amine coating outside the Flory-Stockmayer gelability window 1/((f-1)(g-1)) <= r <= (f-1)(g-1), i.e. the documented index gap is network-formation-threatening.
model_assumptions: Ideal Flory-Stockmayer statistics: equal and independent reactivity of all amine hydrogens, no intramolecular cyclization, no etherification side reaction. Real epoxy-amine systems show primary/secondary substitution effects and cycles that DELAY the gel point (raise p_gel), so the ideal window used here is the conservative bound in the gelability direction; the containment verdict is additionally protected by the quantified headroom P*.
non_circularity: Equations (1)-(4), both KAT anchors, the sqrt corner-shift corollary, and the closed-form headroom P* are published polymer physics re-derived here from first principles; g and AHEW derive purely from IUPAC-2021 atomic weights + published formulas; DGEBA f=2 / EEW=170.21 are portfolio-locked molar-mass facts. Only on-disk fixture bytes are consumed; the shipped constraint-envelope-oracle-v1 evaluate_gate is reused solely to re-confirm the excursion corners PASS the actual contract. Distinct from amphora-molecule-role-ranker's Flory/Macosko-Miller receipts, which rank molecule-level gelation capability; this study bounds the physical severity of the ENVELOPE tolerance gap.

purpose: Bound the physical severity of the envelope->stoichiometric-index gap documented by stoichiometric-index-equivalents-v1: map the shipped +/-5% per-part mass envelope's worst-case index corners through the Flory-Stockmayer gelation criterion for DGEBA(f=2) + amine(g=active-H) stepwise networks and test H0 = 'the envelope can defeat gelability'.

theory_constants.shift_invariance_note: p_gel scales as sqrt(r), so the envelope-induced gel-point conversion shift is EXACTLY sqrt of the index corner factor, independent of EEW, AHEW, g and the nominal masses -- the sqrt-corollary of the excursion-invariance theorem.

theory_reference: Flory, P.J., 'Molecular Size Distribution in Three Dimensional Polymers I-III', J. Am. Chem. Soc. 63 (1941) 3083-3100, DOI 10.1021/ja01856a061 (gel-point criterion, p_c=1/(f-1) anchors).
Stockmayer, W.H., 'Theory of Molecular Size Distribution and Gel Formation in Branched-Chain Polymers', J. Chem. Phys. 11 (1943) 45-55, DOI 10.1063/1.1723803 (A_f+B_g gel point p_A p_B (f-1)(g-1)=1).
Odian, G., 'Principles of Polymerization', 4th ed., Wiley 2004, Ch.2.10/2.12, ISBN 978-0471274001 (stoichiometric-imbalance form p_gel = sqrt(r/((f-1)(g-1))), gelability at full conversion).
Lee, H. & Neville, K., 'Handbook of Epoxy Resins', McGraw-Hill 1967, Ch.5-6 (amine-H functionality of epoxy hardeners; f=2 for DGEBA).
IUPAC 2021 conventional standard atomic weights (C 12.011, H 1.008, N 14.007); amphora KAT molar-mass DGEBA EEW=170.21 g/eq (n=0).
